title: Abt-Buy product matching (DeepMatcher test split)
decision: whether two product records from two shops describe the same product

source.name: Abt-Buy (Köpcke, Thor, Rahm, VLDB 2010) in the textual version and split of DeepMatcher (Mudgal et al., SIGMOD 2018)
source.version: archive files dated 2018-06-04; Datasets.md at commit a89ffe6cd246f690afd2772e47eb071741160f16

licence: DeepMatcher Datasets.md: no licence stated for the data (repository code: BSD 3-Clause); origin of the records, Leipzig benchmark page: "These datasets are made available by the database group of Prof. Erhard Rahm under the Creative Commons license" (link target: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
labels: mixed: matches from the reference mapping of the original authors; non-matches are blocked candidate pairs that are not in the mapping
notes: 108 matches + 892 non-matches: the class ratio of the test split (206 matches in 1,916 pairs), drawn per class (seed 20261007). record_a is the row of tableA.csv (left), record_b the row of tableB.csv (right), fields name, description, price; values are the preprocessed (lower-cased, tokenised) strings of the DeepMatcher files, empty where the source is empty. The pairs are candidates that survived DeepMatcher's blocking; a pair is a match if it is in the reference mapping of the original authors, otherwise a non-match. The split is DeepMatcher's random 3:1:1 split of the pairs, so the same records also occur in the public training and validation pairs. Licence: the origin (Leipzig) is under CC BY 4.0, the DeepMatcher files state none: kept as rebuild script only. Decontamination against the authors' training data (scan of 7 October 2026, 1,546,178 training records): 4 of 1000 items removed because a text field of the item occurs in it; 996 items remain.
